title: “Never Again” a Massacre Like the One at Tlatelolco, Sheinbaum Says; Underscores Díaz Ordaz’s Responsibility
author: Arturo Sánchez Jiménez and Alma E. Muñoz
content:
_This article by[Arturo Sánchez Jiménez and Alma E.
Muñoz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez%20Jim%C3%A9nez%20y%20Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz)
originally appeared in the [October 2, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/02/politica/nunca-mas-una-
masacre-como-la-de-tlatelolco-sheinbaum-subraya-responsabilidad-de-diaz-
ordaz), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. Fifty-eight years after the Tlatelolco massacre, the federal
government reiterated this Friday that **the main person responsible for the
repression of the[1968 student
movement](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/01/politica/la-cia-se-
enfoco-en-grupos-estudiantiles-antes-y-despues-de-tlatelolco) was the then-
president of the Republic and commander of the Army, Gustavo Díaz Ordaz**, and
called for the State to "never again" repress a social movement.

President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo opened her morning press conference at the
National Palace with the rallying cry "October 2 is not forgotten" and
recalled the date as "one of the most painful episodes in the history of
Mexico. The repression of a student movement in the Plaza de Tlatelolco."

The president recalled that two years ago, at the start of her administration,
a statement was read that was later published in the Official Gazette of the
Federation (DOF), recognizing that the main person responsible for the events
was "the one who was then commander of the National Army, the then-president
of the Republic of the United Mexican States."

Sheinbaum Pardo emphasized that this responsibility was "**acknowledged by
himself at different moments of his life after having been president**."

> Our solidarity always with those who lived through it at that time, their
> families, and never again. Never again a repression by the State of a social
> movement.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum
